reason: This capacitor is only connected between the output node and an internal node (net44) that is otherwise tied to VSS through R2, so it mainly adds an extra pole/zero (compensation or filtering) rather than being required for the DC biasing or basic differential-to-single-ended operation.
impact_estimate: Low–Medium: DC gain/bias largely unchanged; transient stability/settling and noise filtering may change, so keep it if compensation/stability is critical.

reason: R2 primarily provides a DC reference for net44 (used only by C0). If C0 is removed, net44 becomes unused and R2 can be deleted as well without affecting the signal path or biasing of the amplifier core.
impact_estimate: Low (assuming C0 is also removed): no meaningful change to amplifier behavior; if C0 remains, deleting R2 leaves net44 floating which can cause unpredictable transient behavior.

reason: R3 behaves as an explicit output load/bleeder to ground; most amplifier cores will still function without it, and the output node will still be defined by the active devices and any remaining feedback/load elements (e.g., R0/R1 network).
impact_estimate: Low–Medium: output DC operating point and small-signal gain may shift depending on how heavily the original design relied on this load; safe to remove if an external load is assumed or if R0/R1 already provide a DC path.
